name: Degrowth
summary: Degrowth holds that rich countries should plan a democratic, equitable reduction of energy and material throughput, because green growth has not delivered absolute decoupling. It pairs this with redistribution, shorter and shared work, decommodified public services and localised provision. It is explicitly not recession or austerity and not a demand for poor countries to shrink.
scope: The academic and activist degrowth movement of the 2000s to 2020s as set out by Hickel, the Degrowth.info editorial collective and Parrique's survey of the degrowth literature. It excludes steady-state economics and green-growth positions, and answers only where these sources state a position.
